objective: Replace finite-sample generalization for the frozen normalized-rule graph behavior with a universal proof over its actual contract boundary.

frozen_boundary.inputs: finite structured requirements plus normalized applicable rules plus input schema
frozen_boundary.upstream_excluded: semantic extraction of unstated or implicit rules
frozen_boundary.owned_behavior: deterministic requirement-to-intermediate-to-output graph materialization and fail-closed structural validation after rule normalization

theorem.domain: Every finite admissible instance at the frozen normalized-rule boundary.
theorem.termination: Pending-rule count is a natural-number ranking function. In a finite acyclic dependency graph with declared external inputs, every nonempty pending subgraph has at least one ready rule. Each successful iteration removes at least one rule. If no rule is ready while pending is nonempty, the instance is cyclic or unresolved and the compiler fails closed.
theorem.soundness: Every emitted derived node and edge is copied from one declared normalized rule only after exact dependency and type/dimension validation. Operator identity is opaque input data; operator semantics are not invented by the compiler.
theorem.coverage: Every applicable requirement must have a traced consumer, excluded requirements require justification, declared invariants are preserved, and every required output must be materialized.
theorem.scope_binding: The independently verified V2 scope gate reports admissible substitution with zero unresolved dimensions for this exact behavior boundary.
theorem.ceiling: Therefore every admissible in-domain instance satisfies the frozen graph-materialization behavior and every structurally invalid instance fails closed. Success on the frozen behavior relation is 1, its theoretical maximum.
